# Turnstone Chrome extension — MANIFEST V3 SIDE PANEL

**Status: built and verified.** [`dist/`](dist/) is a loadable unpacked extension, regenerated by
[`build.js`](build.js) from the app in the repository root.

## What it is

A Manifest V3 extension whose **entire UX is Chrome's Side Panel** — the task-card sidebar only.
**There is no iframe workflow in this port at all.** Instead of hosting pages, the queue drives the
browser.

## The core interaction

- Links always open as **real browser tabs** (`chrome.tabs.create`).
- **Selecting a card switches the browser to that card's tab** — and if the tab is already open,
  it is activated instead of reloaded (`chrome.tabs.get` → `chrome.tabs.update`). That is the same
  "focus, never duplicate" rule the web app's iframe tab bar follows, re-pointed at real tabs.
- A tab that closes stops counting as open, so the next click opens a fresh one.
- The toolbar **badge** shows tasks still to do, readable with the panel shut.
- **Right-click any link → "Add link to Turnstone"** appends it to the open queue; if no queue is
  open it starts one, and if the panel is shut the link is stashed in `chrome.storage` and picked up
  on the next open.

## What mirrors the web version

Everything the sidebar does, because it *is* the sidebar: cards, ✓ Complete / ↺ Incomplete, notes,
search, sorting, column presets, exports, auto-open and auto-advance, and the file round-trip
resume. Exports go through `chrome.downloads`. Picking a file keeps live write-back (Chromium),
exactly as in the web app; queue, presets and the open file persist per browser in IndexedDB, so
they survive closing the panel.

## What is different, and why

| Web app | Extension | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Tabbed iframe workspace | **Removed** | A side panel is ~360 px of chrome, not a viewport. Links become real tabs instead. |
| Three open modes | **One** (`Real browser tabs`) | The other two describe surfaces this port does not have. |
| PWA install prompt, `beforeunload` guard | **Removed** | An install prompt and a "you have unsaved changes" dialog belong to a web origin; the panel is already installed and its state is a database, not a tab. |
| `?file=` deep links | **Removed** | A side panel has no URL bar. Pasting a URL still works. |

## Layout

```
extension/
  build.js            # generator: extracts + patches app.html, asserts every anchor
  manifest.json       # the manifest source (paths resolve inside dist/)
  src/
    background.js     # MV3 service worker: context menu, badge, pending-link stash
    panel-bridge.js   # chrome.tabs open/focus, badge, context-menu adds  (inlined into sidepanel.js)
    chrome-mock.js    # test double for the extension APIs                (harness only)
  dist/               # GENERATED — load THIS folder with "Load unpacked"
  README.md
```

`dist/` is committed on purpose: it is the artifact people load, the same way
`turnstone-standalone.html` and `ports/bookmarklet/dist/*.txt` are committed.

## Building

```bash
node ports/extension/build.js           # → ports/extension/dist/
node ports/extension/build.js --check    # verify dist matches app.html, write nothing
```

`app.html` is patched, never forked. Every edit is asserted against an exact anchor, so a change
upstream **fails the build** rather than silently shipping a panel that no longer matches the app.
The build also asserts the end state: no inline script survived, `window.open` and `openInIframe`
are gone, `chrome.tabs.create` and `chrome.downloads.download` are present, the panel CSS is in
place, and every asset the page references is packaged. `--check` is a strict byte comparison.

## Verifying it without installing it

Two generated harnesses carry the parts a plain `http` load cannot reach:

| Harness | Proves |
|---|---|
| `dist/panel-csp.html` | The panel runs under the extension page CSP (`script-src 'self'; object-src 'self'`) with **no inline script and no eval** — the browser applies that policy as a response header, so the harness restates it as a meta tag. |
| `dist/panel-test.html` | The extension-only half: a mock of `chrome.tabs` / `chrome.action` / `chrome.storage` / `chrome.downloads` (`src/chrome-mock.js`) records what the panel asked for. It is how "one tab per card, second click switches instead of duplicating", the badge message, the `chrome.downloads` export and the context-menu append were checked outside `chrome://extensions`. `?pending=<url>` simulates a link queued while the panel was shut. |

Neither harness is referenced by the manifest; Chrome ignores both.

## Install

1. `chrome://extensions` → **Developer mode**
2. **Load unpacked** → choose `ports/extension/dist`
3. Click the toolbar icon

Needs **Chromium 114+** (Side Panel API): Chrome and Edge. Firefox cannot load this folder — MV3
with a side panel is not implemented there; use the standalone build or the web app instead.
